atoms.b: ((++Colons Semi-colons)) (:) are punctuation marks used to divide sentences.
They can be used to introduce a ((++list,_series_or_quote person,_animal_or_object)) when following an independent clause.
They can also be used to show ((++emphasis confusion)) or bring two ((++independent dependent)) clauses together.

instruction.text: Drag the colon to the correct spot in the sentence.

atoms.b: My family has three dogs((:)) Ollie, Rocco and Gigi.
atoms.sound: My family has three dogs:  Ollie, Rocco and Gigi.

atoms.b: Sasha happily replied to the text from her best friend((:)) “Thanks for always being there for me!”
atoms.sound: Sasha happily replied to the text from her best friend: “Thanks for always being there for me!”

atoms.b: I have one goal for this year((:)) to muster up the courage to ride a roller coaster.
atoms.sound: I have one goal for this year: to muster up the courage to ride a roller coaster.

atoms.b: I have a fun fact for you ((:)) crocodiles cannot stick out their tongues.
atoms.sound: I have a fun fact for you: crocodiles cannot stick out their tongues.

instruction.text: Select the sentence with the correct use of colons.

b: There is only one thing left: to do we need to hoover the living room.
++There is only one thing left to do: we need to hoover the living room.
atoms.sound: There is only one thing left to do: we need to hoover the living room.

b: ++Ella has four cousins: Lee, Kelsey, Rami and Theo.
Ella has: four cousins: Lee, Kelsey, Rami and Theo.
atoms.sound: Ella has four cousins: Lee, Kelsey, Rami and Theo.

b: ++He emailed his colleague: “The workshop will be on Wednesday.”
He emailed his colleague “:The workshop will be on Wednesday.”
atoms.sound: He emailed his colleague: “The workshop will be on Wednesday.”

atoms.a: I have one wish for this holiday: to swim with dolphins.

feedback.wrong: Remember, colons are only used to introduce a quote if the quote is preceded by an independent clause.
